skillsSummary: 1. Perform computer troubleshooting2. Repair faulty components.
3. Test computer component functionality4. Perform computer maintenance

criteria: 1.1 User data is assessed as per workplace procedures.
1.2 Computer problems are identified as per the assessed user data.
1.3 Solution to the problem is determined as per workplace procedure.
2.1 Computer components for replacement are selected as per the workplace procedure.
2.2 Tools for repairing or replacing are assembled as per the workplace procedure.
2.3 Safety procedures are observed as per workplace procedures.
2.4 Faulty computer components are repaired or replaced as per the manufacturer’s manual.
2.5 Obsolete or faulty computer components are disposed as per workplace procedures.
3.1 Computer is switched on for POST test as per workplace procedure.
3.2 Computer component test is performed as per workplace procedure.
3.3 Computer component’s functionality report is generated as per workplace procedure.
4.1 Computer maintenance is scheduled as per the workplace procedure.
4.2 Computer maintenance is performed as per the workplace procedure.
4.3 Computer maintenance report is generated as per workplace procedure.

schedule.sessionTitle: Introduction to Computer Repair & User Data Assessment
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Define computer repair and maintenance concepts.  b. Explain the importance of assessing user data in troubleshooting.  c. Document initial faulty computer user data according to workplace procedures.
trainerActivities: - Deliver a lecture introducing computer repair and maintenance fundamentals.  - Facilitate a group discussion on various methods for assessing user data during fault diagnosis.  - Guide trainees through practical exercises on documenting user reported issues.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the introductory lecture and engage in Q&A.  - Contribute to the group discussion, sharing insights on user data collection.  - Practice documenting simulated user data using provided templates.  Assignment: Research and list common computer repair and maintenance definitions.
resourcesAndRefs: - Textbooks, unit description document  - Whiteboard and markers  - Computer systems (for scenario demonstration)
assessments: - Oral questioning  - Observation of group discussion participation  - Review of documented user data exercises

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Describe various computer troubleshooting approaches.  b. Identify basic computer hardware faults from symptoms.  c. Apply methods for gathering comprehensive information from users.
trainerActivities: - Present different systematic troubleshooting methodologies (e.g., top-down, bottom-up).  - Showcase common hardware fault symptoms through practical demonstrations on faulty machines.  - Coordinate role-playing scenarios to practice effective information gathering from simulated users.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the presentation, discussing the pros and cons of different approaches.  - Observe demonstrations of hardware faults and actively identify symptoms.  - Engage in role-playing, practicing communication and questioning techniques to gather user information.  Assignment: Develop a flowchart for a chosen troubleshooting approach.
resourcesAndRefs: - Troubleshooting guides, online resources  - Faulty computer systems for demonstration  - Communication skills handouts
assessments: - Short quiz on troubleshooting approaches  - Observation of symptom identification  - Peer assessment during role-play

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Analyze collected user data to infer potential problems.  b. Formulate hypotheses about the root cause of computer issues.  c. Determine a logical solution based on identified problems and data analysis.
trainerActivities: - Lead a guided analysis session using documented user data case studies.  - Facilitate a brainstorming activity for developing problem hypotheses based on symptoms.  - Present decision-making frameworks for determining the most effective solution.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the data analysis, identifying key information and patterns.  - Contribute to the brainstorming activity, proposing and discussing potential causes.  - Apply decision-making frameworks to select appropriate solutions for presented scenarios.  Assignment: Analyze a given case study and propose a solution.
resourcesAndRefs: - Case study handouts  - Whiteboard for brainstorming  - Decision-making matrices
assessments: - Discussion participation  - Review of hypotheses formulation  - Evaluation of proposed solutions

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Classify common computer hardware faults and their manifestations.  b. Identify appropriate remedies for specific hardware failures.  c. Differentiate between software and hardware related problems.
trainerActivities: - Deliver an interactive lecture on various hardware components and their typical failure modes.  - Demonstrate basic hardware fault remedies (e.g., reseating RAM, checking power connections).  - Lead a comparative analysis activity distinguishing hardware from software symptoms.
traineeActivities: - Engage in the interactive lecture, asking questions and discussing fault types.  - Observe the demonstrations, then practice simple remedies on training machines.  - Participate in the analysis activity, categorizing and discussing different problem types.  Assignment: Create a table listing 5 common hardware faults and their remedies.
resourcesAndRefs: - Hardware components (working and faulty)  - Diagnostic software  - Textbooks and online repair manuals
assessments: - Oral assessment on fault classification  - Practical observation of remedy application  - Group activity output

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Develop a plan for testing troubleshooting hypotheses.  b. Execute tests to confirm or refute a hypothesis.  c. Document the identified problem and the testing process accurately.
trainerActivities: - Guide trainees in developing systematic testing plans for pre-defined troubleshooting scenarios.  - Supervise practical sessions where trainees execute diagnostic tests using tools and software.  - Instruct on best practices for documenting problem identification, tests performed, and outcomes.
traineeActivities: - Collaborate in small groups to develop testing plans for given scenarios.  - Perform diagnostic tests on computer systems, observing and recording results.  - Practice documenting the entire problem identification and testing process comprehensively.  Assignment: Document a simulated troubleshooting process from hypothesis to identified problem.
resourcesAndRefs: - Diagnostic tools (multimeter, POST card)  - Diagnostic software (HWMonitor, MemTest86)  - Documentation templates
assessments: - Review of testing plans  - Practical assessment of test execution  - Evaluation of documentation quality

schedule.sessionTitle: Review of Troubleshooting Techniques & Computer Systems
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Summarize key troubleshooting techniques and procedures.  b. Identify main components of various computer systems.  c. Discuss the interaction between different computer components during operation.
trainerActivities: - Lead a comprehensive review session covering all troubleshooting concepts from Element 1.  - Conduct a hands-on session where trainees identify and label internal computer components.  - Facilitate a discussion on component interdependencies and how failures in one affect others.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the review, contributing to summaries and asking clarifying questions.  - Disassemble and reassemble computer systems, correctly identifying and labeling components.  - Engage in the discussion, explaining component interactions and potential fault propagation.  Assignment: Prepare a short presentation on a specific computer system's component interaction.
resourcesAndRefs: - Disassemblable computer systems  - Component diagrams  - Review questionnaires
assessments: - Oral review questions  - Practical identification of components  - Discussion participation

schedule.sessionTitle: Manufacturer's Warranty & Time Management in Troubleshooting
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain manufacturer's warranty requirements related to repair activities.  b. Apply time management techniques to optimize troubleshooting processes.  c. Critically evaluate troubleshooting scenarios to prioritize tasks.
trainerActivities: - Present a lecture on common warranty policies and their implications for repair.  - Lead a workshop on time management strategies specifically for computer repair tasks.  - Introduce complex troubleshooting case studies and guide trainees in critical thinking for prioritization.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the lecture, discussing different warranty scenarios and asking questions.  - Practice applying time management techniques to simulated repair timelines.  - Analyze case studies, making critical decisions on task prioritization and resource allocation.  Assignment: Draft a time management plan for a given complex troubleshooting task.
resourcesAndRefs: - Sample warranty documents  - Time management tools/templates  - Advanced troubleshooting case studies
assessments: - Oral questioning on warranty knowledge  - Review of time management plans  - Group discussion on case study analysis

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Develop a systematic plan for complex troubleshooting tasks.  b. Apply problem-solving methodologies to resolve computer issues.  c. Utilize planning skills to anticipate potential challenges in repair.
trainerActivities: - Guide trainees through creating detailed troubleshooting plans for multi-faceted problems.  - Facilitate interactive problem-solving exercises using various techniques (e.g., divide and conquer).  - Lead a discussion on proactive planning to mitigate risks in the repair process.
traineeActivities: - Collaborate in groups to construct comprehensive troubleshooting plans for provided scenarios.  - Engage in problem-solving activities, applying learned methodologies to solve simulated faults.  - Contribute to the discussion, proposing strategies for effective risk anticipation and mitigation.  Assignment: Create a detailed troubleshooting plan for a simulated 'dead computer' scenario.
resourcesAndRefs: - Complex fault scenarios  - Problem-solving worksheets  - Project planning tools
assessments: - Assessment of troubleshooting plans  - Observation of problem-solving techniques  - Oral contribution to discussion

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Demonstrate effective communication with users about computer problems.  b. Translate technical jargon into understandable language for non-technical users.  c. Manage user expectations and provide clear updates on repair progress.
trainerActivities: - Conduct role-playing exercises simulating various customer interaction scenarios.  - Provide feedback and coaching on clear, concise, and empathetic communication.  - Discuss strategies for setting realistic expectations and delivering bad news constructively.
traineeActivities: - Participate actively in role-playing, practicing communication with simulated users.  - Receive and integrate feedback to improve their communication style.  - Contribute to discussions on effective client management and managing difficult conversations.  Assignment: Prepare a script for explaining a complex computer issue to a non-technical client.
resourcesAndRefs: - Role-play scripts  - Communication skills checklists  - Customer service guidelines
assessments: - Performance during role-playing  - Peer and trainer feedback  - Oral questioning on communication strategies

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Perform systematic fault diagnosis on a range of computer issues.  b. Utilize diagnostic tools and software effectively to identify problems.  c. Apply learned troubleshooting skills to solve real-world simulated scenarios.
trainerActivities: - Set up various computer systems with pre-introduced faults for practical diagnosis.  - Guide trainees in using a variety of diagnostic hardware and software tools.  - Oversee independent troubleshooting exercises, providing support and correction as needed.
traineeActivities: - Conduct systematic fault diagnosis on assigned faulty computer systems.  - Practice using diagnostic tools and software to pinpoint the root causes of issues.  - Independently apply troubleshooting techniques to resolve simulated problems.  Assignment: Diagnose a given faulty computer system and submit a preliminary fault report.
resourcesAndRefs: - Faulty computer systems (various issues)  - Comprehensive set of diagnostic tools and software  - Workshop manuals
assessments: - Practical demonstration of fault diagnosis  - Observation of tool usage  - Review of diagnostic reports

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Analyze advanced and intermittent computer troubleshooting scenarios.  b. Develop creative and efficient solutions for complex or rare faults.  c. Learn from case studies to improve problem-solving adaptability.
trainerActivities: - Present and dissect complex troubleshooting case studies with challenging or intermittent faults.  - Facilitate group discussions and brainstorming for non-standard solutions.  - Encourage trainees to research and share examples of unusual computer problems and their resolutions.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the analysis of advanced case studies, identifying subtle clues and potential issues.  - Contribute to group brainstorming, proposing innovative diagnostic and repair strategies.  - Research and present findings on unusual computer problems, enhancing collective knowledge.  Assignment: Prepare a presentation on an advanced troubleshooting case study from your research.
resourcesAndRefs: - Advanced troubleshooting textbooks  - Online technical forums and resources  - Whiteboard for solution mapping
assessments: - Participation in case study discussions  - Quality of proposed solutions  - Presentation of research findings

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Consolidate all theoretical knowledge acquired in Element 1.  b. Practice identifying and solving a variety of troubleshooting problems efficiently.  c. Reflect on common troubleshooting errors and best practices.
trainerActivities: - Conduct a thorough review of all learning outcomes, knowledge, and skills for Element 1.  - Administer a short practical troubleshooting scenario to gauge understanding.  - Lead a reflective discussion on lessons learned and areas for continuous improvement.
traineeActivities: - Actively participate in the review, clarifying any remaining doubts and consolidating understanding.  - Perform the short practical scenario, applying learned skills and reflecting on their approach.  - Contribute to the reflective discussion, sharing insights and identifying personal growth areas.  Assignment: Complete a self-assessment checklist for Element 1 competency.
resourcesAndRefs: - Element 1 review materials  - Short practical scenario setups  - Self-assessment checklists
assessments: - Oral questioning  - Trainer observation during practical scenario  - Review of self-assessment

schedule.sessionTitle: Introduction to Repairing Faulty Components & Component Selection
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Outline the process of repairing and replacing faulty computer components.  b. Identify various types of computer hardware components.  c. Describe factors to consider when selecting replacement computer components.
trainerActivities: - Present an overview of Element 2: Repairing Faulty Components, detailing the repair workflow.  - Showcase different categories of computer hardware components (input, output, storage, processing, communication).  - Lead a discussion on critical factors for component selection, such as compatibility, cost, and availability.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the overview, asking questions about the repair lifecycle.  - Inspect and identify various physical computer components, distinguishing their functions.  - Contribute to the discussion, analyzing real-world scenarios for component selection.  Assignment: Research and list three reputable vendors for computer hardware parts.
resourcesAndRefs: - Computer hardware components (samples)  - Manufacturer's specifications  - Textbooks on computer architecture
assessments: - Oral questioning on component types  - Observation of component identification  - Group discussion participation

schedule.sessionTitle: Computer Parts Acquisition & Repair Tools Assembly
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain the process of acquiring computer hardware components.  b. Identify essential tools for computer repair and replacement.  c. Assemble a basic computer repair toolkit for various tasks.
trainerActivities: - Deliver a presentation on sourcing and acquiring computer hardware components, including ordering procedures.  - Demonstrate the correct identification and use of essential hand tools for computer repair.  - Supervise trainees as they assemble their personal or shared repair toolkits.
traineeActivities: - Engage in the presentation, discussing procurement challenges and best practices.  - Observe the demonstrations, then practice handling and identifying repair tools.  - Independently or in pairs, assemble a functional computer repair toolkit.  Assignment: Compile a checklist of tools required for common computer repair tasks.
resourcesAndRefs: - Computer parts catalogs, online supplier websites  - Assorted computer repair tools (screwdrivers, pliers, etc.)  - Toolkit organizer
assessments: - Oral questioning on acquisition methods  - Practical identification of tools  - Observation of toolkit assembly

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify and correctly use specialized computer repair tools.  b. Implement essential safety procedures during computer repair.  c. Select appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for different tasks.
trainerActivities: - Demonstrate the proper use of specialized tools such as chip extractors, hex wrenches, and Torx screwdrivers.  - Present and explain critical safety procedures, including electrical safety and anti-static precautions.  - Guide trainees in selecting and donning various PPE (overall, gloves, anti-static wrist strap, mat).
traineeActivities: - Observe demonstrations and then practice using specialized repair tools.  - Participate in discussions on safety procedures, identifying potential hazards.  - Practice selecting and correctly using PPE for simulated repair environments.  Assignment: List all anti-static equipment and explain their function.
resourcesAndRefs: - Specialized computer repair tools  - Safety manuals, workplace safety posters  - Various PPE items
assessments: - Practical demonstration of tool use  - Oral questioning on safety procedures  - Observation of PPE selection and use

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Classify different types of fires relevant to a computer repair environment.  b. Identify appropriate fire extinguishers for each class of fire.  c. Outline emergency procedures and first aid protocols in a workshop setting.
trainerActivities: - Deliver a lecture on fire classifications (A, B, C, D, K) and their causes in an ICT workshop.  - Demonstrate the correct use of various fire extinguishers and explain their mechanisms.  - Present and discuss emergency contact information, evacuation plans, and basic first aid for common injuries.
traineeActivities: - Engage in the lecture, discussing fire hazards and prevention in an ICT context.  - Observe fire extinguisher demonstrations, then identify the correct type for different scenarios.  - Participate in a simulated emergency drill, practicing evacuation and first aid response.  Assignment: Develop a fire safety checklist for a computer repair workshop.
resourcesAndRefs: - Fire safety posters, fire extinguisher samples  - First aid kit, emergency contact list  - Workplace emergency response plan
assessments: - Oral questioning on fire classifications  - Practical identification of extinguisher types  - Participation in emergency drill

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Develop contingency measures for unexpected repair challenges.  b. Interpret computer components instruction manuals effectively.  c. Perform the safe and systematic disassembly of computer components.
trainerActivities: - Lead a scenario-based discussion on developing backup plans for repair obstacles (e.g., unavailable parts).  - Guide trainees through interpreting various manufacturer's manuals and technical diagrams.  - Demonstrate the correct and systematic disassembly of a desktop and laptop computer.
traineeActivities: - Contribute to the discussion, proposing and evaluating contingency plans for given scenarios.  - Practice reading and understanding component manuals for specific repair tasks.  - Observe the disassembly demonstration, then perform guided disassembly of computer systems.  Assignment: Select a computer component and outline its disassembly steps based on its manual.
resourcesAndRefs: - Various computer instruction manuals  - Computer systems for disassembly practice  - Contingency planning templates
assessments: - Group discussion contributions  - Practical interpretation of manuals  - Observation of disassembly technique

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Systematically reassemble computer components after repair.  b. Apply basic repair techniques for common component issues.  c. Verify correct component installation through visual inspection.
trainerActivities: - Demonstrate the systematic reassembly of a computer system, emphasizing proper connections.  - Guide trainees through practical exercises on basic repair techniques (e.g., cleaning, cable management).  - Instruct on crucial visual inspection points to confirm proper component seating and connections.
traineeActivities: - Observe the reassembly demonstration, then perform guided reassembly of computer systems.  - Practice basic repair techniques on various components, ensuring functionality.  - Conduct visual inspections of reassembled systems, identifying any installation errors.  Assignment: Reassemble a disassembled computer system and ensure all connections are secure.
resourcesAndRefs: - Disassembled computer systems  - Repair toolkit  - Assembly checklists
assessments: - Practical assessment of reassembly  - Observation of repair techniques  - Quality check of visual inspections

schedule.sessionTitle: Replacing Faulty RAM and Storage Devices
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Diagnose and confirm faulty RAM modules.  b. Replace RAM modules and various storage devices (HDDs, SSDs) safely and correctly.  c. Configure new storage devices for basic operation (e.g., partitioning, formatting).
trainerActivities: - Demonstrate the diagnosis of faulty RAM using diagnostic software and physical inspection.  - Guide trainees through the step-by-step process of replacing RAM, HDDs, and SSDs.  - Instruct on basic partitioning and formatting procedures for new storage devices.
traineeActivities: - Use diagnostic software to identify faulty RAM in simulated scenarios.  - Observe demonstrations, then practice replacing RAM and storage devices in various computer systems.  - Perform basic partitioning and formatting on newly installed storage devices.  Assignment: Install an operating system on a newly installed and configured storage drive.
resourcesAndRefs: - Working and faulty RAM modules  - Various HDDs/SSDs, SATA/power cables  - Operating system installation media, diagnostic software
assessments: - Practical diagnosis of RAM  - Observation of component replacement  - Verification of storage device configuration

schedule.sessionTitle: Power Supply Unit (PSU) Diagnosis and Replacement
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify symptoms of a faulty Power Supply Unit (PSU).  b. Perform safe testing of a PSU using a multimeter or PSU tester.  c. Safely replace a faulty PSU with a compatible new unit.
trainerActivities: - Present common symptoms and troubleshooting steps for a failing PSU.  - Demonstrate how to safely test PSU voltages using a multimeter or a dedicated PSU tester.  - Guide trainees through the safe removal and installation of various types of PSUs.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the discussion on PSU failure symptoms and diagnostic approaches.  - Observe demonstrations, then practice safe PSU testing on non-live and live (supervised) systems.  - Practice replacing PSUs in different computer cases, ensuring all connections are secure.  Assignment: Research and compare different PSU efficiency ratings (e.g., 80 Plus Bronze, Gold).
resourcesAndRefs: - Working and faulty PSUs  - Multimeters, PSU testers  - Various computer cases and power cables
assessments: - Oral questioning on PSU symptoms  - Practical demonstration of PSU testing  - Observation of PSU replacement procedure

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Recognize signs of a failing motherboard.  b. Follow proper procedures for removing and installing a motherboard.  c. Connect all peripheral and power cables to a new motherboard correctly.
trainerActivities: - Deliver a lecture on motherboard components and common failure points, including POST codes.  - Demonstrate the meticulous process of removing and installing a motherboard, emphasizing screw patterns and standoffs.  - Supervise trainees as they practice connecting all necessary cables (power, data, front panel) to a new motherboard.
traineeActivities: - Engage in the lecture, discussing motherboard diagnostics and failure symptoms.  - Observe the motherboard replacement demonstration, then perform guided removal and installation.  - Practice connecting all internal cables to a motherboard, referring to manuals as needed.  Assignment: Create a step-by-step guide for replacing a motherboard.
resourcesAndRefs: - Various motherboards (working and non-working)  - Computer cases, standoffs, screws  - Manufacturer's manuals, POST code charts
assessments: - Oral questioning on motherboard issues  - Practical observation of motherboard replacement  - Verification of cable management and connections

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Troubleshoot issues related to input, output, and communication devices.  b. Safely replace common input/output devices (keyboards, mice, monitors).  c. Install and configure network interface cards (NICs) and Wi-Fi adapters.
trainerActivities: - Present troubleshooting techniques specific to I/O and communication devices.  - Guide trainees through practical exercises for replacing external I/O devices and internal expansion cards.  - Instruct on basic driver installation and network configuration for new communication components.
traineeActivities: - Participate in troubleshooting discussions for peripheral issues.  - Practice replacing various input/output devices and internal expansion cards.  - Perform driver installation and basic network configuration for installed NICs/Wi-Fi adapters.  Assignment: Configure a wireless network connection after installing a new Wi-Fi adapter.
resourcesAndRefs: - Various input/output devices (keyboards, mice, monitors)  - Network interface cards (NICs), Wi-Fi adapters  - Driver CDs/USB, network cables
assessments: - Practical diagnosis of I/O issues  - Observation of component replacement  - Verification of network connectivity

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify different CPU socket types and compatible processors.  b. Safely install or replace a CPU and apply thermal paste correctly.  c. Install and test CPU cooling systems (heatsinks, fans).
trainerActivities: - Deliver a lecture on CPU architectures, socket types, and compatibility.  - Demonstrate the delicate process of CPU installation, emphasizing proper alignment and thermal paste application.  - Guide trainees through installing and testing various CPU cooling solutions.
traineeActivities: - Engage in the lecture, discussing CPU specifications and compatibility.  - Observe the CPU installation, then perform guided CPU replacement and thermal paste application.  - Practice installing and verifying the functionality of CPU heatsinks and fans.  Assignment: Research the latest CPU technologies and their cooling requirements.
resourcesAndRefs: - Various CPUs and motherboards (for socket types)  - Thermal paste, cleaning supplies  - Assorted CPU coolers (air and AIO liquid coolers)
assessments: - Oral questioning on CPU compatibility  - Practical demonstration of CPU installation  - Verification of cooling system functionality

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Differentiate between integrated and dedicated graphics solutions.  b. Safely install and secure a dedicated graphics card in a PCIe slot.  c. Install graphics drivers and perform basic display configuration.
trainerActivities: - Present a comparison of integrated vs. dedicated graphics, discussing their applications.  - Demonstrate the physical installation of a graphics card, including power connections and securing mechanisms.  - Instruct on downloading and installing appropriate graphics drivers and setting up multi-monitor configurations.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the discussion, identifying scenarios for using different graphics solutions.  - Observe the GPU installation, then practice installing graphics cards in available systems.  - Perform driver installation and configure display settings for optimal performance.  Assignment: Troubleshoot a 'no display' issue after a GPU installation.
resourcesAndRefs: - Various graphics cards (working and non-working)  - Computer systems with PCIe slots  - Graphics driver installation media, display cables
assessments: - Oral questioning on graphics types  - Practical demonstration of GPU installation  - Verification of display output and driver status

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain the environmental impact of improper e-waste disposal.  b. Identify different categories of e-waste and associated hazards.  c. Describe proper disposal methods for obsolete or faulty computer components.
trainerActivities: - Deliver a lecture on the environmental and health hazards of e-waste, including pollution.  - Present various types of e-waste (e.g., batteries, circuit boards) and their toxic components.  - Discuss and demonstrate different proper disposal methods and local regulations for e-waste.
traineeActivities: - Engage in the lecture, discussing the importance of responsible e-waste management.  - Participate in an activity to categorize various computer parts into e-waste types.  - Contribute to the discussion, researching local e-waste disposal centers and practices.  Assignment: Create a poster or infographic on the dangers of e-waste and proper disposal.
resourcesAndRefs: - E-waste samples (non-toxic)  - Environmental protection guidelines  - Local e-waste recycling center information
assessments: - Oral questioning on e-waste impact  - Group activity on waste categorization  - Discussion participation

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Distinguish between various advanced e-waste recycling and disposal technologies.  b. Perform data sanitization techniques to ensure data privacy before disposal.  c. Understand legal and ethical considerations in component disposal.
trainerActivities: - Present advanced e-waste processing techniques (e.g., material recovery, hazardous waste treatment).  - Demonstrate software-based and physical data sanitization methods for storage devices.  - Facilitate a discussion on data protection laws and ethical responsibilities in disposing of IT assets.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the presentation, discussing the complexities of advanced recycling.  - Observe demonstrations, then practice data sanitization on sample storage devices.  - Engage in the discussion, analyzing case studies related to data breaches from improper disposal.  Assignment: Research and compare three data sanitization standards (e.g., DoD 5220.22-M).
resourcesAndRefs: - Data sanitization software (e.g., DBAN)  - Physical shredders (demo/video), degaussers  - Data protection regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.)
assessments: - Oral questioning on disposal methods  - Practical demonstration of data sanitization  - Participation in ethical discussion

schedule.sessionTitle: Review of Element 1 & 2 for CAT 1 Preparation
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Systematically review all theoretical concepts related to troubleshooting and repair.  b. Confidently answer questions pertaining to Element 1 and Element 2 performance criteria.  c. Strategize effectively for approaching both written and practical assessment components of CAT 1.
trainerActivities: - Conduct a focused Q&A session, addressing any remaining uncertainties about Elements 1 and 2.  - Administer a comprehensive mock written test mirroring the CAT 1 format and difficulty.  - Provide a walkthrough of the practical CAT 1 environment and expectations, including rubric review.
traineeActivities: - Actively participate in the Q&A, posing questions and consolidating their understanding.  - Attempt the mock written test under timed conditions, identifying areas for final review.  - Engage in the walkthrough, clarifying practical setup and understanding assessment criteria.  Assignment: Review personal strengths and weaknesses based on mock test results and prepare a study plan for CAT 1.
resourcesAndRefs: - Comprehensive study guide for Elements 1 & 2  - Mock CAT 1 papers (written)  - Practical assessment rubric and checklist
assessments: - Performance in mock written test  - Active participation in Q&A  - Readiness assessment through direct questioning

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Demonstrate theoretical understanding of computer troubleshooting and repair principles.  b. Apply knowledge of safety procedures, component selection, and fault diagnosis.  c. Articulate solutions to common computer issues and proper disposal methods.
trainerActivities: - Administer the Written Continuous Assessment Test 1.  - Invigilate the examination to ensure fair and compliant testing conditions.  - Collect all examination papers upon completion.
traineeActivities: - Attempt the Written CAT 1, adhering to all instructions and time limits.  - Demonstrate their theoretical knowledge and understanding of Elements 1 and 2.  - Submit their completed examination papers.
resourcesAndRefs: - CAT 1 examination papers  - Pens and other authorized stationery
assessments: - Written CAT 1 score  - Adherence to exam procedures

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Practically perform computer troubleshooting steps on a faulty system.  b. Accurately repair or replace faulty computer components as per manufacturer's manual.  c. Observe safety procedures and perform safe disposal of obsolete components.
trainerActivities: - Administer the Practical Continuous Assessment Test 1.  - Observe and assess trainees' practical troubleshooting, repair, and disposal skills against a rubric.  - Provide necessary equipment and ensure a safe testing environment.
traineeActivities: - Attempt the Practical CAT 1 by diagnosing, repairing/replacing, and disposing of components.  - Demonstrate proficiency in tool usage, safety adherence, and repair/replacement techniques.  - Complete and submit required documentation for the practical task.
resourcesAndRefs: - Faulty computer systems/components for practical assessment  - Diagnostic toolkits, repair toolkits, PPE, disposal containers  - Practical assessment rubric and documentation templates
assessments: - Practical CAT 1 performance (pass/fail, score based on rubric)  - Accuracy of fault identification, component replacement, and disposal methods

schedule.sessionTitle: Introduction to Computer Component Functionality Testing & POST
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Explain the importance of testing computer components for functionality.  b. Describe the Power-On Self-Test (POST) process.  c. Identify common POST codes and their meanings.
trainerActivities: - Deliver an introductory lecture on why and when component functionality testing is crucial.  - Present the POST sequence, explaining what happens during startup and common beeps/codes.  - Demonstrate how to interpret POST codes using a POST card or motherboard diagnostic LEDs.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the lecture, discussing the benefits of thorough component testing.  - Engage in an interactive session, identifying and interpreting various POST codes.  - Observe demonstrations, then practice using a POST card to diagnose startup issues.  Assignment: Research and list 10 common POST beep codes and their corresponding faults.
resourcesAndRefs: - Computer systems (working and non-booting)  - POST cards, motherboard manuals  - Textbooks on computer architecture
assessments: - Oral questioning on testing importance  - Observation of POST code identification  - Group discussion on startup diagnostics
